title: The associated graded ring of an ideal is a commutative graded ring and an A/J-algebra

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma 05GH (lemma-completion-Noetherian, line 23011), lines 23032-23035: '$\bigoplus I^n/I^{n+1}$' used as a ring and an $R/I$-algebra without proof; Algebra, Section 00JL (section-graded, line 13200) for graded rings; Artin approximation, Section 07XA (artin-section-approximation), artin.tex line 1268, the notation $\text{Gr}_I(A)=\bigoplus I^n/I^{n+1}$

proof.text: From the ideal-product definition in [def-weil-pbc-algebra-hom-quotient], $J^{r+1}\subseteq J^r$: each generator $xy$ with $x\in J^r,y\in J$ lies in the ideal $J^r$, and hence so does the ideal it generates. Also $J^1=AJ=J$, since $aj\in J$ and $j=1j$. Thus $J^{n+1}$ really is a submodule of $J^n$ and $G_0=A/J$ as an abelian group by [def-weil-pbc-quotient-module].

source.place: Tags 05GH (lemma-completion-Noetherian, associated graded ring in the proof) and 00JL (section-graded); elementary construction of the multiplication omitted there

proof.text: For every $r\ge1$, $J^r$ consists of finite sums of products of $r$ elements of $J$. The induction starts at $r=1$; for the successor, generators of $J^rJ$ are products of such sums with one element of $J$, and ring coefficients can be absorbed into that last element of $J$. Conversely every such product belongs to $J^rJ$. Expanding products of the two finite sums gives $ab\in J^{n+m}$ whenever $a\in J^n,b\in J^m$; if either index is zero this is just closure of an ideal under multiplication by $A$. In particular $J^{n+1}J^m\subseteq J^{n+m+1}$ and $J^nJ^{m+1}\subseteq J^{n+m+1}$.

source.place: Tags 05GH (lemma-completion-Noetherian, associated graded ring in the proof) and 00JL (section-graded); elementary construction of the multiplication omitted there

proof.text: Write $[a]_n$ for the coset of $a\in J^n$ in $G_n$. Define $\mu_{n,m}([a]_n,[b]_m)=[ab]_{n+m}$. This lies in the stated quotient by step 2. If representatives are replaced by $a+u,b+v$, where $u\in J^{n+1},v\in J^{m+1}$, the difference is $ub+av+uv$. The first two terms lie in $J^{n+m+1}$ by step 2, and the third lies in $J^{n+m+2}\subseteq J^{n+m+1}$ by step 1. The cosets are therefore equal. Surjectivity of both quotient maps in [def-weil-pbc-quotient-module] proves uniqueness of a map with this representative formula.

source.place: Tags 05GH (lemma-completion-Noetherian, associated graded ring in the proof) and 00JL (section-graded); elementary construction of the multiplication omitted there

proof.text: Using the quotient addition and scalar operations of [def-weil-pbc-quotient-module], the identities $(a+a')b=ab+a'b$, $a(b+b')=ab+ab'$, $(ca)b=c(ab)=a(cb)$ and $0b=a0=0$ in $A$ prove biadditivity, $A$-linearity in each variable, and vanishing with a zero argument. On representatives, $(ab)c=a(bc)$ proves $\mu_{n+m,r}(\mu_{n,m}(x,y),z)=\mu_{n,m+r}(x,\mu_{m,r}(y,z))$ after identifying the equal degrees; $ab=ba$ gives commutativity, and $1a=a=a1$ gives the two degree-zero unit identities. Quotient-map surjectivity extends these identities to all $x,y,z$.

proof.text: For $\xi,\eta\in G$ use the convolution in the statement as the definition of their product. Each component is a finite sum (there are only $k+1$ pairs of natural numbers with $n+m=k$). If $S,T$ are the finite supports of $\xi,\eta$ from [def-weil-pbc-direct-sum-modules], step 4 implies that the product is supported in the finite set $\{n+m:n\in S,m\in T\}$. Hence it is in $G$. For single-component families the only possibly nonzero summand is the pair $(n,m)$, giving $\iota_n(x)\iota_m(y)=\iota_{n+m}(\mu_{n,m}(x,y))$ component by component.

source.place: Tags 05GH (lemma-completion-Noetherian, associated graded ring in the proof) and 00JL (section-graded); elementary construction of the multiplication omitted there

proof.text: The addition of $G$ is already an abelian group operation by [def-weil-pbc-direct-sum-modules]. In each degree $k$, biadditivity from step 4 gives $\sum_{n+m=k}\mu(\xi_n,\eta_m+\zeta_m)=\sum_{n+m=k}\mu(\xi_n,\eta_m)+\sum_{n+m=k}\mu(\xi_n,\zeta_m)$, proving left distributivity. Swapping $(n,m)$ with $(m,n)$ and using homogeneous commutativity proves $\xi\eta=\eta\xi$, and consequently right distributivity as well. Equality of components is equality of the families defining $G$.

source.place: Tags 05GH (lemma-completion-Noetherian, associated graded ring in the proof) and 00JL (section-graded); elementary construction of the multiplication omitted there

proof.text: For associativity fix $k$. Distribute the inner finite sums using step 4 to obtain $((\xi\eta)\zeta)_k=\sum_{n+m+r=k}\mu_{n+m,r}(\mu_{n,m}(\xi_n,\eta_m),\zeta_r)$ and $(\xi(\eta\zeta))_k=\sum_{n+m+r=k}\mu_{n,m+r}(\xi_n,\mu_{m,r}(\eta_m,\zeta_r))$. These are sums over the same finite set of triples: the first grouping uses the uniquely determined intermediate degree $n+m$, the second $m+r$. Homogeneous associativity from step 4 equates every summand. Thus every component, and hence both families in [def-weil-pbc-direct-sum-modules], agrees.

source.place: Tags 05GH (lemma-completion-Noetherian, associated graded ring in the proof) and 00JL (section-graded); elementary construction of the multiplication omitted there

proof.text: Set $e=\iota_0([1]_0)$. In $(e\xi)_k$ all terms vanish except $(0,k)$ and its value is $\mu_{0,k}([1]_0,\xi_k)=\xi_k$ by step 4. Commutativity gives $\xi e=\xi$ too. Together with steps 5--7 and the direct-sum abelian group structure [def-weil-pbc-direct-sum-modules], this proves precisely the commutative unital ring laws for the specified convolution; step 5 proves its grading law.

source.place: Tags 05GH (lemma-completion-Noetherian, associated graded ring in the proof) and 00JL (section-graded); elementary construction of the multiplication omitted there

proof.text: Under $G_0=A/J$ from step 1, $\mu_{0,0}([a]_0,[b]_0)=[ab]_0$ is exactly the quotient-ring multiplication of [def-weil-pbc-algebra-hom-quotient]. The componentwise inclusion $\iota_0$ of [def-weil-pbc-direct-sum-modules] preserves addition, step 5 shows it preserves multiplication, and step 8 shows it preserves the unit. It is injective since its degree-zero component is the original element: $\iota_0(x)=\iota_0(y)$ implies $x=y$ by taking that component. This proves clause (3)'s ring-homomorphism assertion.

source.place: Tags 05GH (lemma-completion-Noetherian, associated graded ring in the proof) and 00JL (section-graded); elementary construction of the multiplication omitted there

proof.text: The ring homomorphism of step 9 makes $G$ an $A/J$-algebra by the definition in [def-weil-pbc-algebra-hom-quotient]; explicitly its scalar action is $\overline a\cdot\xi=\iota_0(\overline a)\xi$, whose module axioms are the ring distributive, associative and unit laws already proved. For $x\in J^n$, step 5 gives $\iota_0([a]_0)\iota_n([x]_n)=\iota_n([ax]_n)$. If $a$ is changed by $j\in J$, then $jx\in J^{n+1}$ by step 2, so the formula depends only on $a\bmod J$. Each image $\iota_n(G_n)$ is closed under addition and additive inverses by its componentwise definition [def-weil-pbc-direct-sum-modules], and the displayed formula proves closure under every $A/J$ scalar. Therefore it is an $A/J$-submodule of $G$.
